rationale: This is a cosmetic re-weighting of the archived "Kinked financing slope by cash quality" (identical financing legs, only the quality scalar swapped), and the composite weight is internally redundant because NEG((ib−oancf)/at) and oancf/at both load on operating cash flow, so the "three independent quality dimensions" claim is overstated.

A legitimate and cleanly executed conditioning test of a known portfolio-composition concern (sector-loaded tails), though it is still the incumbent kink with demeaned inputs, and note that industry-demeaning the financing flow redefines the kink point so that firms merely below the peer payout norm are now classified into the "raising" leg — the sign logic survives but the economic interpretation shifts.

The expression is internally consistent (surplus×buffer minus deficit×buffer-scarcity, correctly positive-signed) and the FMB-strong/alpha-weak diagnosis genuinely motivates the kink, but it is a mechanical crossing of two archived signals rather than a new economic channel, so the incremental information content is modest.

The "use of funds" channel is absent from the archive and the non-negative rank weight does neutralize internally funded growth as claimed, but the base variable is the classic working-capital accrual (Sloan) and its interaction with external financing is close to the published external-financing/accrual literature, so the test must show incremental power over a plain accrual control to be interesting.

A genuinely distinct economic mechanism (debt-overhang/distress resolution) that correctly diagnoses why the archived coverage-weighted debt signal put the most weight where deleveraging is least informative; the only inconsistency is that the multiplicative form applies the same weight to the issuance tail, whereas the hypothesis is stated only about the repayment tail and would be more faithfully expressed as a kink.

Testing the second moment of financing flows is a legitimately new dimension and the sign logic is correct, but the doubly-ranked non-negative product saturates at zero for any firm with decent cash flow or stable financing, so the long leg will be a large tied mass and the spread will be driven almost entirely by the short leg — plus the five-year VOL window will bite into coverage.
